title: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia, Smudge Cells, CD5 CD23, and Follicular Lymphoma t(14;18)

steps.tx: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and small lymphocytic lymphoma represent different manifestations of the same indolent non-Hodgkin B-cell neoplasm, differing only by tissue distribution. Marked by an absolute clonal peripheral blood lymphocytosis exceeding five thousand mature B-cells per microliter sustained for at least three months, **chronic lymphocytic leukaemia** is the most prevalent leukaemia among adults in Western nations. Microscopic examination of blood films shows monotonous, small, mature-appearing lymphocytes with round nuclei, coarsely clumped soccer-ball chromatin, and inconspicuous cytoplasm.
steps.say: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia is the most frequent leukaemia in elderly adults across Western countries. The World Health Organization defines CLL by finding a persistent clonal B-cell lymphocytosis of at least five thousand cells per microliter in peripheral blood. Under the microscope, the neoplastic cells look deceptively normal: small, mature lymphocytes with scantly visible cytoplasm and densely condensed chromatin resembling the dark pattern on a soccer ball.

vis.alt: Peripheral blood smear in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia showing mature lymphocytes and smudge cells
vis.caption: CLL peripheral blood smear with mature lymphocytes and smudge cells.

steps.tx: A characteristic morphological feature on peripheral blood films of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia is the abundant presence of **smudge cells**, historically termed Gumprecht shadows or basket cells. Smudge cells are artefactual remnants of fragile neoplastic lymphocytes that rupture during the mechanical shear stress of spreading the blood drop across a glass slide. Although smudge cells carry no intrinsic biological malignancy, mixing one drop of bovine albumin with four drops of blood prior to film preparation preserves cell membrane integrity, preventing lysis.
steps.say: A classic diagnostic clue on a CLL blood film is the appearance of smudge cells, also called Gumprecht shadows. These pale, smeared cellular remnants are not distinct biological entities, but artifacts created when mechanically fragile leukemic lymphocytes burst under the shear stress of spreading the blood smear. Adding a drop of bovine albumin to the blood sample stabilizes the cell membranes and eliminates smudge cell distortion.

left.title: Smudge Cell Artifact
points: Eliminated by adding bovine serum albumin

right.title: Intact Neoplastic Lymphocyte
points: Surface expression of CD19, CD5, and CD23

steps.tx: Diagnostic confirmation of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia requires multiparameter flow cytometry demonstrating a pathognomonic immunophenotypic profile. Clonal B-cells co-express pan-B markers CD19 and CD20 (characteristically dim) alongside the T-cell activation antigen **cluster of differentiation 5** and the activation antigen CD23. Crucially, neoplastic cells exhibit weak, dim surface immunoglobulin expression demonstrating light chain restriction (kappa or lambda). This aberrant co-expression of CD5 and CD23 conclusively differentiates CLL from mantle cell lymphoma, which is CD23 negative and cyclin D1 positive.
steps.say: Flow cytometry is the definitive test to confirm chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. Neoplastic B-cells display a unique antigen signature: they co-express standard B-cell markers like CD19 with the T-cell marker CD5 and the activation antigen CD23. Furthermore, they express characteristically dim surface immunoglobulin with monoclonal light chain restriction. The presence of CD23 and absence of cyclin D1 reliably distinguishes CLL from aggressive mantle cell lymphoma.

Demonstrates clonality and light chain restriction
Classic flow gating parameter in CLL

steps.tx: Clinical risk stratification in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia utilizes two widely accepted systems: the American **Rai staging system** and the European Binet staging system. Rai stage 0 is defined by isolated blood and marrow lymphocytosis. Stage I adds lymphadenopathy, Stage II incorporates splenomegaly or hepatomegaly, Stage III is defined by anaemia with haemoglobin under eleven grams per deciliter, and Stage IV indicates thrombocytopenia with platelet count under one hundred thousand. Stages III and IV constitute advanced disease carrying poor baseline survival.
steps.say: Clinicians grade CLL severity using the Rai and Binet staging systems based entirely on physical exam and standard blood counts. Under the Rai classification, stage zero is isolated lymphocytosis. Stages one and two add lymphadenopathy and organomegaly. Stages three and four denote bone marrow failure with anaemia below eleven grams per deciliter or thrombocytopenia below one hundred thousand per microliter, indicating advanced disease requiring treatment.

steps.tx: Asymptomatic early-stage chronic lymphocytic leukaemia does not benefit from immediate chemotherapy, adhering to a strict **watch-and-wait management strategy**. Randomized clinical trials demonstrate that early intervention in Rai stage 0 or Binet stage A fails to improve overall survival and exposes patients to unnecessary toxicity. Treatment initiation is reserved for active disease: progressive bone marrow failure with worsening anaemia or thrombocytopenia, massive symptomatic splenomegaly extending six centimeters below costal margin, bulky progressive lymphadenopathy, refractory autoimmune haemolytic anaemia, or constitutional B symptoms.
steps.say: Asymptomatic patients with early-stage CLL should not receive immediate treatment. Large clinical trials have repeatedly proven that chemotherapy in early disease does not extend life and only produces drug toxicity. Instead, we adopt a watchful waiting approach, checking counts every few months. Treatment is triggered only by active disease manifestations: progressive marrow failure, massive symptomatic splenomegaly, rapidly doubling lymphocytosis, or refractory autoimmune cytopenias.

left.title: Watch-and-Wait Criteria
points: Asymptomatic Rai 0 or Binet A disease
Routine clinical review every 3 to 6 months

right.title: Active Treatment Indications
points: Unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or fever

steps.tx: Accounting for twenty percent of all non-Hodgkin lymphomas, **follicular lymphoma** is the second most frequent adult lymphoid malignancy. Derived from germinal centre B-cells, it exhibits a nodular, follicular architectural pattern that effaces normal lymph node tissue. Under high magnification, the neoplastic follicles are composed of a mixture of small cleaved cells with indented nuclei termed centrocytes and larger non-cleaved cells with vesicular chromatin and prominent nucleoli termed centroblasts. Unlike reactive follicles, neoplastic follicles lack tingible-body macrophages and display attenuated mantle zones.
steps.say: Follicular lymphoma is the second most common adult non-Hodgkin lymphoma and represents the quintessential indolent lymphoid cancer. Biopsy reveals a monotonous nodular proliferation of neoplastic follicles that effaces normal lymph node architecture. Inside follicles, a mixture of small cleaved centrocytes and larger centroblasts proliferates. Crucially, neoplastic follicles lack tingible-body macrophages and polarized dark-light zones, demonstrating loss of normal germinal center control.

vis.alt: Follicular lymphoma lymph node histology showing a nodular follicle centre pattern with a t(14;18) inset
vis.caption: Follicular lymphoma lymph node histology showing a nodular follicle centre pattern with a t(14;18) inset. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The genetic hallmark present in eighty-five to ninety percent of follicular lymphomas is the balanced reciprocal **translocation t(14;18)(q32;q21)**. This structural rearrangement moves the BCL2 proto-oncogene from chromosome 18 into juxtaposition with the immunoglobulin heavy-chain enhancer on chromosome 14. Constitutive overexpression of BCL2 protein suppresses the physiological apoptotic death that germinal centre B-cells normally undergo during somatic hypermutation, leading to relentless accumulation of long-lived clonal centrocytes and centroblasts within follicular structures.
steps.say: Nearly ninety percent of follicular lymphomas are initiated by the reciprocal translocation t(14;18), which relocates the BCL2 gene from chromosome eighteen adjacent to the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus on chromosome fourteen. This rearrangement drives continuous, high-level expression of BCL2 protein. Because BCL2 suppresses apoptosis, germinal center B-cells that should normally die if they fail antigen selection survive indefinitely, accumulating as indolent follicular lymphoma.

steps.tx: In two to eight percent of patients with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, the indolent disease undergoes an abrupt histological transformation termed **Richter transformation**, most frequently evolving into an aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Patients present with sudden, discordant clinical deterioration characterized by rapid asymmetrical enlargement of a single lymph node group, new systemic B symptoms, and an acute spike in serum lactate dehydrogenase. Positron emission tomography demonstrates localized intense standardized uptake value exceeding 5, and median survival is under one year.
steps.say: Richter transformation describes the sudden histological evolution of indolent CLL into an aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, occurring in roughly five percent of patients. Clinically, suspect Richter transformation when a patient experiences rapid, asymmetrical enlargement of a single lymph node site accompanied by severe fever, weight loss, and an acute jump in serum LDH. PET scanning shows intensely hot lesions with SUVs exceeding five, and the transformed disease is notoriously refractory to chemotherapy.

quiz.q: Which flow cytometric immunophenotypic profile is pathognomonic of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia?
options: CD19 positive, CD5 positive, CD23 positive, Cyclin D1 negative
CD19 positive, CD5 positive, CD23 negative, Cyclin D1 positive
CD19 positive, CD10 positive, BCL2 positive, CD5 negative
CD3 positive, CD4 positive, CD8 negative, CD25 positive
quiz.explain: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia is defined by the co-expression of CD5 and CD23 on clonal CD19-positive B-cells with dim surface immunoglobulin, whereas mantle cell lymphoma is CD23 negative and cyclin D1 positive.

quiz.q: Which chromosomal translocation drives the molecular pathogenesis of follicular lymphoma?
quiz.explain: Follicular lymphoma is characterized in up to 90% of cases by the t(14;18)(q32;q21) translocation that places the anti-apoptotic BCL2 gene under the IGH enhancer.

quiz.q: What histological and clinical event defines Richter transformation in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia?
options: Evolution of indolent CLL into aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
Transformation of CLL into acute promyelocytic leukaemia with DIC
Progression of CLL into primary myelofibrosis with dry marrow tap
Development of severe pure red cell aplasia responsive to steroids
quiz.explain: Richter transformation refers to the sudden development of an aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (or rarely Hodgkin lymphoma) in a patient with pre-existing CLL.
